features.title: Native Settings shell, ported
features.summary: The sidebar Settings trigger, connection recovery pill, Desktop update indicator, section navigation, General section, onboarding coordinator and Mod+, shortcut of the native Settings shell, served by this bundle with the native row switched off.
failureModes: When the running DSH ships another version of the native Settings package, the Host warns at boot and General shows the running version, so the port is refreshed instead of drifting silently.

The native welcome notice stores its acknowledgement in the switched-off row's namespace, so the shell ports that step and keeps the acknowledgement in its own namespace; someone who acknowledged the native notice sees it once more.

verification.testName: matches the native Settings package this workspace builds against

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Native Settings shell, ported renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: One dockable Settings hub with real navigation and forms
features.summary: The New tab chooser offers one Settings hub with actual section navigation, search and native/plugin forms. Leaf sections remain registered for saved layouts and explicit links but are hidden from primary suggestions. The authorized shell renderer and ConfigForm remain the owners. Workbench pane chrome is mandatory; hidden right-pane tabs retain their state. It is the same grouped page as the stage page, for free-docking layouts.
failureModes: Without a mounted workbench the sources remain registered but no docked panel is shown.
A removed settings section or namespace unregisters; an existing panel never falls through to another section.
Build and browser verification must include the workbench registry dependency and the shared stylesheet owner.

verification.testName: offers one Settings hub and keeps individual sections/pages registered but hidden from the chooser
calls the declaring renderer with only the requested section and closes that panel occurrence

telemetry.reason: Client-only projection of existing settings sources into presentation panels; ConfigForm operations retain their existing Host API spans.

features.title: DSH release notice and TL;DR
features.summary: The Settings trigger marks a new public DSH release, and General compares it with the installed Host version, shows a concise English TL;DR across newer releases, links to the official notes, and lets the user dismiss that release notice.
features.currentSurface: sidebar: Settings trigger release mark › General
failureModes: GitHub is unavailable or returns an invalid payload; Settings stays usable and offers a manual retry.
The installed version is absent from the bounded release history; the plugin reports that comparison is unknown instead of guessing.
Release notes are bounded and rendered as escaped plain text; malformed or HTML content cannot inject client markup.

externalDependencies.boundary: Host-only GET to the fixed public deepseek-harness releases endpoint; response data is schema-validated, bounded, and rendered as untrusted text.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: release-status.test.ts injects a fixed fetch response and covers release ordering, version matching, English note extraction, redirects, and malformed payloads.

verification.testName: lists releases after the installed version and keeps their links on GitHub

telemetry.testName: records a dsh release check span with whether an update exists

features.title: One Settings page in the stage
features.summary: Settings has one place: a page in the stage (plans/ade-ux §4.6). The rail, the gear, the palette, Mod+, and other plugins' open requests all open it; the former dialog, expanded dialog and side-panel presentations are gone, and a request that still names one opens the page. With main-tabs it gets a tab like any other page; picking that tab or reloading onto it reopens Settings, leaving it closes Settings.
reach: fill combobox "Search the command palette" "Settings: General"
features.currentSurface: settings: the Settings page in the stage
failureModes: With no other tab left, main-tabs keeps showing Settings: it cannot show an empty main view.
A plugin that still dispatches dshfiles:open-settings with surface modal gets the page; there is no dialog to open.

verification.testName: opens in the stage and closes when the main view leaves it

telemetry.reason: Client-only: the Settings page renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: Settings grouped by task, with deep links
features.summary: Every native section and plugin settings page sits in one task group (General, Models & accounts, Agents, Tools & MCP, Projects & workspaces, Hosts & network, Security, Notifications, Plugins, About; unknown ones under Other) under a person's name, never a package id. AI accounts appears once: its section, its plugin settings and a link to the accounts page. MCP servers, Secrets, Hosts and the AI accounts page are entries that open the page their plugin owns. Every Jev setting sits under Tools & MCP › Jev, and Layout (fixed or free docking) under General. Plugin pages say they apply to every project and thread: no setting stores a per-project or per-thread value yet.
reach: fill combobox "Search the command palette" "Settings: General"
features.currentSurface: settings: task groups in the Settings navigation
failureModes: A section or namespace nobody placed shows under Other with its own label until the group map in src/settings-groups.ts places it.
A linked page whose plugin is not loaded is left out rather than offered as a dead link.
Backlog and Memory still store their own Jev key: Tools & MCP › Jev shows both together until one shared key exists.

Titles, descriptions, key paths, page and group names match, and key bindings by command name or keys; hidden and secret fields never do.

features.title: Search section controls and open them at the control
features.summary: Controls that live Settings sections publish as search entries (dshx settings.section metadata.searchEntries) are found while their sections stay unmounted, listed under their section; picking one opens that section with target set to the entry id, and the section scrolls to and focuses it. General publishes its coding-view switch. The read-only settings_list tool searches the same entries for the Agent.

A section registered imperatively must publish its own entries with publishSettingsSearchEntries.

features.title: Set the Jev key once
features.summary: Settings › Tools & MCP › Jev leads with one Key: a secret:ALIAS reference (Secret Catalog picker) that Backlog triage and Memory's signal gates both resolve on the Host. Each plugin's earlier key stays stored but hidden as the fallback while the shared key is empty, and is copied into an empty shared key once, never over a set one. Backlog's Jev section and Memory's review link here.

configuration.constraints: Secret Catalog reference only (secret:ALIAS or secret:ALIAS@env); resolves on the Host. Empty falls back to each plugin's earlier key, then TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

failureModes: A Host without settings-shell's namespace keeps each plugin reading its own earlier key and the environment.
When Backlog and Memory held different earlier keys, the first adopted one becomes shared; the other stays stored in its plugin and is used again if the shared key is cleared.

verification.testName: copies a plugin key into an empty shared key once
never overwrites a shared key that is already set
loses a race to a concurrent write instead of overwriting it
leads the Jev entry with the one shared key, titled Key, before the plugins that use it

telemetry.reason: A settings field plus a one-time settings write through DSH's settings forms on Host start; no fetch, socket, process or long job. The Jev calls that use the key keep their jev classify span.
